headline: August 20: Presidential election to be held in Bangladesh
summary: The Election Commission has announced the schedule for the presidential election, with polling scheduled for August 20.
details: The Election Commission (EC) announced that the presidential election will be held on August 20, with polling taking place from 2:00pm to 5:00pm.
Nomination papers must be submitted by August 13 between 10:00am and 4:00pm, with the scrutiny of nomination papers beginning on August 16.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed announced the schedule at the commission's headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.
The schedule was announced in accordance with the Presidential Election Act, 1991, following consultations between the chief election commissioner and the Speaker of parliament.
The EC has received the electoral roll comprising the 350 members of parliament from the Parliament Secretariat.
The commission has held a meeting to finalise preparations and will complete remaining administrative procedures in line with the announced schedule.
caption:
Bangladesh's presidential election is set for August 20.

EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed announced the schedule at the commission's headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.

The schedule was announced in accordance with the Presidential Election Act, 1991, following consultations between the chief election commissioner and the Speaker of parliament.

The EC has received the electoral roll comprising the 350 members of parliament from the Parliament Secretariat.

The commission has held a meeting to finalise preparations and will complete remaining administrative procedures in line with the announced schedule.

headline_marked: 109* for Miraz: [[Vice-captain hits century]] in Australia practice match
headline: 109* for Miraz: Vice-captain hits century in Australia practice match
summary: Mehidy Hasan Miraz rescued Bangladesh from a precarious 110/6 to reach 263 all out in a three-day warm-up fixture in Darwin.
details: Vice-captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz struck a fighting, unbeaten 109 off 141 deliveries to rescue Bangladesh on the opening day of a three-day practice match against a Cricket Australia XI.
Bangladesh struggled early after electing to bat, slumping to 110 for six as the top order failed to capitalize on their time in the middle.
Miraz led a spirited recovery, sharing valuable lower-order partnerships to steer the team to a total of 263 all out in 75.5 overs.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto contributed 37 runs, while opener Shadman Islam scored 31.
For the hosts, off-spinner Corey Rocchiccioli was the standout bowler, claiming six wickets for 83 runs.
This century serves as a timely confidence boost for Miraz ahead of the two-Test series against Australia starting later this month.
The three-day fixture in Darwin is Bangladesh's only warm-up match, providing the batting unit a chance to adapt to Australian conditions.
caption:
From 110/6 to 263! Mehidy Hasan Miraz delivers a masterclass century in Australia.

Vice-captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz struck a fighting, unbeaten 109 off 141 deliveries to rescue Bangladesh on the opening day of a three-day practice match against a Cricket Australia XI.

Bangladesh struggled early after electing to bat, slumping to 110 for six as the top order failed to capitalize on their time in the middle.

Miraz led a spirited recovery, sharing valuable lower-order partnerships to steer the team to a total of 263 all out in 75.5 overs.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto contributed 37 runs, while opener Shadman Islam scored 31.

For the hosts, off-spinner Corey Rocchiccioli was the standout bowler, claiming six wickets for 83 runs.

This century serves as a timely confidence boost for Miraz ahead of the two-Test series against Australia starting later this month.

The three-day fixture in Darwin is Bangladesh's only warm-up match, providing the batting unit a chance to adapt to Australian conditions.
